source.title: Trajectory Soup: Pushing the Compute-Scaling Frontier of LLM Mid-training via Diverse Trajectories
source.authors: Zhehao Huang; Chang-Xin Tian; Qing-Yuan Yang; Kun-Long Chen; Zi-Qi Liu; Zhi-Qiang Zhang; Xiao-Lin Huang; Jun Zhou

page_placements.theme: Parallel training trajectories and checkpoint averaging change compute returns

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. There are minor text-extraction artifacts in equations and flattened tables, plus appendix placeholders; these do not make the study unreadable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests compute-related performance trends using downstream accuracy in mid-training, rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy or the parameter/token scaling measurements in the original studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream aggregate-accuracy outcomes for compute budgets and fits accuracy-versus-compute curves. It does not report held-out cross-entropy scaling. Cited scaling-law findings are background, not results of this study. Theoretical loss identities are assumptions and derivations, not empirical measurements of the claim's pretraining-loss versions.
record.test_reason: This is a model-merging method paper. It borrows the compute-allocation framing and a power-law functional form from Kaplan/Hoffmann only to summarise its own results. Every result is downstream accuracy of one fixed-size model (or a 2B model) as mid-training tokens grow, and most compare Trajectory Soup with other merging baselines. No result varies parameters, pretraining tokens or pretraining compute. No result reports held-out pretraining loss scaling or downstream prediction from pretraining scale or loss. The one result that touches scaling-law territory is that serial mid-training accuracy saturates and declines. That is a related but different construct (repeated-corpus mid-training of a fixed model), so it is recorded under fits_no_version, not as a test of V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that serial mid-training saturates. Spreading the budget over compatible branches and averaging validation-selected checkpoints within and across them gives a single model with higher aggregate downstream accuracy than the best single-trajectory merge, at matched and expanded budgets, and the advantage largely survives a shared SFT. They also note that the gains are small (tenths of a point), that selection and reported scores share one validation signal, and that compute accounting omits storage, validation and search costs.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates mid-training compute allocation across branches and downstream accuracy, rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss against parameter count, tokens, or compute as in the original scaling-law studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with budget mode (Limited or Extended), trajectory count, model scale, learning-rate schedule, branch recipe, checkpoint selection, and whether evaluation occurs before or after SFT. The raw single-trajectory curve saturates or declines, whereas the Trajectory Soup frontier continues to improve in the reported range.

fits_no_version.finding: For a fixed 7.9B-total MoE, downstream accuracy along a serial mid-training run improves early, then plateaus and declines. An inverse-power fit to 17 raw checkpoints (25B–425B tokens) has R2=0.594, and later checkpoints scatter downward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy during mid-training of a fixed model on a fixed corpus saturates and can decline with more serial tokens, rather than following a power law.

fits_no_version.finding: The best merged-checkpoint frontier (validation-selected) across multiple branches fits an inverse power law in total mid-training compute (R2=0.965) and keeps rising to 2400B-equivalent tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parallel-branch compute plus checkpoint averaging yields a smoother accuracy-vs-compute curve in mid-training than serial training.

record.problems: The study measures aggregate benchmark accuracy rather than held-out cross-entropy. The raw accuracy fit has R2 = 0.594 and its displayed extrapolation extends beyond the fitted range. Tabulated outcomes have no reported error bars. The authors note that compute accounting omits checkpoint storage, validation passes, search costs, and accelerator-utilization differences; selection and reported accuracy are not fully independent. The supplied model description is not independently verified through a public model release.
record.rows_left_out: Only the Overall Average accuracy was retained for the tabulated strategy comparisons. Separate capability-category scores in Tables 2–4 and the additional coefficient/selection ablations in Table 5 were not extracted because they are not the primary aggregate scaling measure. Figure-only curve values without explicit numeric statements were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits predicting held-out loss of larger runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token split. Allocation is across trajectory count and length within mid-training.
No other modality is tested. Mid-training/SFT accuracy is not fitted for the claim's power-law loss form.
No downstream performance vs model scale or pretraining loss. Only mid-training token budget on fixed-size models is varied.
No comparison of fitting choices for loss laws or the compute-optimal split.

record.verdict_notes: The power-law fits are fitted to downstream accuracy against mid-training FLOPs of a fixed model, explicitly 'inspired by' Kaplan/Hoffmann. They are a presentation device for the method, not a test of the scaling-law claim. The reader's V6 labels conflate method superiority (merging vs single run) with scaling predictability and should be dropped. The Single-Trajectory Merge reference is a different branch in Table 2 (EXP1) than in Table 3 (EXP2). The Extended comparisons are not compute-matched.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits predicting held-out loss of much larger runs.
The study allocates mid-training compute across trajectory count and length, but does not fit loss-minimising parameter and token counts as powers of compute.
No fixed-parameter-count comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices.
No test of a common power-law form for held-out loss across modalities or training regimes.

Tests aggregate downstream accuracy against mid-training compute and reports post-training comparisons; it does not test prediction from pretraining loss or predict individual downstream tasks from a fitted loss curve.
The reported fits concern downstream accuracy, not held-out loss or the parameter/token compute-optimal split; the study does not compare fitting choices for those original quantities.

relation.reason: Appendix C.1 explicitly borrows the power-law form for empirical accuracy fits that summarize plotted trends; the experiments evaluate trajectory allocation and merging.

tranche.reason: The study borrows the scaling-law compute-allocation framing and inverse-power functional form to summarize its merging method and raw comparator. It reports descriptive downstream-accuracy fits at fixed architecture, rather than independently testing the catalog's loss laws, compute-optimal parameter/token split, or downstream predictive law.

source_check.notes: The 66.92% raw estimate is extrapolated at one quarter of the compute of the observed 69.03% soup result. Accuracy-based checkpoint and configuration selection is not independent of reported scores; compute accounting excludes validation, search, and storage costs.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Trajectory Soup compute scaling and reported post-SFT comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Aggregate accuracy fits the reported compute trend, and Trajectory Soup results exceed the single-trajectory reference in the listed settings (r4, r5, r9, r10, r12, r13, r15, r17, r19, r20, r21, r22).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Raw serial mid-training scaling after saturation
reader_labels.reason: The raw curve has a comparatively weak fit and the paper reports that it bends over, plateaus, and can decline as training continues (r14, r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Model Soup and the smaller-model Limited comparison
reader_labels.reason: Some expanded Model Soup or Limited results are only slightly above the single-trajectory reference, and Limited Model Soup after SFT is below it (r2, r3, r7, r8, r11, r12).
